[[2015 Maui Invitational Tournament|Maui Invitational tournament]] champions |bowl = [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Elite Eight }} {{2015–16 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kansas]] in the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], which is the Jayhawks 118th basketball season. The Jayhawks played their home games at [[Allen Fieldhouse]]. They were led by 13th year head coach [[Bill Self]] and were members of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. They finished the season 33–5, 15–3 in Big 12 play to win their 12th consecutive regular season Big 12 title. They defeated [[2015–16 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]], [[2015–16 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]], and [[2015–16 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]] to be champions of the [[2016 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]]. They received an automatic bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they were the tournament's overall #1 seed. They defeated [[2015–16 Austin Peay Governors basketball team|Austin Peay]], [[2015–16 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], and [[2015–16 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] to advance to the Elite Eight where they lost to [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]]. The Jayhawks 12 consecutive regular season Big 12 titles was at the time the longest active consecutive conference title streak in the nation, as well as only being one shy of the NCAA record of 13, which is currently held by [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] who won 13 in a row between 1967 and 1979.{{cite web|title=No. 2 Jayhawks beat Texas Tech for Big 12 title share|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400831551|website=ESPN.com}} In July 2015, the Jayhawks represented the [[United States]] at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Summer Universiade|World University Games]] in [[Gwangju]], [[South Korea]]. '''#14'''  |} ===World University Games=== {{main|Basketball at the 2015 Summer Universiade – Men's tournament}} In April 2014, the Kansas basketball team was selected by the United States International University Sports Federation (US-IUSF) to represent the United States in the [[2015 Summer Universiade|2015 World University Games]]. Kansas was selected as the team to represent the U.S. from the schools that expressed interest. This was the second time a college team represented the United States in the World University Games; [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|University of Northern Iowa]] had finished 9th [[Basketball at the 2007 Summer Universiade|in 2007]]. Current university students or recent graduates, born between Jan. 1, 1990, and Dec. 31, 1997, were eligible for the 2015 Games. Only U.S. citizens were eligible for [[United States at the 2015 Summer Universiade|the U.S. team]]; therefore [[Cheick Diallo]], [[Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk]], and Dwight Coleby (from [[Mali]], [[Ukraine]], and [[Bahamas]] respectively) were ineligible. The Kansas travel party, consisting of 12 competitors and 11 staff (23 total), left Lawrence on June 28 and lived in the athlete village throughout the Games. There were two non-Jayhawks on the U.S. roster: guards [[Nic Moore]] of [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]]{{cite web|title=SMU's Nic Moore to play with Kansas team at University Games|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25191847/smus-nic-moore-to-play-with-kansas-team-at-university-games}} and Julian DeBose of [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast]],{{cite web|title=Florida Gulf Coast’s Julian DeBose will join KU for World University Games|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/campus-corner/article25073992.html}} replacing injured Kansas guard Devonte' Graham. Team USA won all their matches in [[Basketball at the 2015 Summer Universiade – Men's tournament|the tournament]], beating Germany 84–77 in double overtime on July 13, 2015, to win the gold medal.
